questions.stem: The Union government's H1 FY27 finances were supported by dividends, profits and disinvestment receipts even as tax collections remained subdued. In this context, consider the following statements. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts excluding borrowings.
Dividends and profits received from the RBI and public sector undertakings are classified as capital receipts in the Union Budget.
Proceeds from disinvestment of government equity in public sector enterprises are classified as capital receipts.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is the standard definition of fiscal deficit. Statement 3 is correct — disinvestment proceeds are capital receipts since they reduce government assets/equity. Statement 2 is wrong: RBI/PSU dividends and profits are non-tax revenue receipts, not capital receipts, since they don't create a liability or reduce an asset.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: How the government finance math looks more challenging in H2 FY27
questions.pyqLink: Tests classification of budget receipts (revenue vs capital), a recurring static theme; similar to UPSC questions on fiscal deficit components.

questions.stem: With reference to India's performance in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI), consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The EPI is published jointly by Yale and Columbia Universities and ranks countries using indicators across multiple issue categories such as air quality, biodiversity and climate policy.
India's poor overall EPI ranking in 2026 was driven by it also ranking among the lowest on air pollution (emissions) control, the same as its air quality ranking.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct and matches the article's description of EPI's publishers and its 47 indicators across 12 issue categories. Statement 2 is incorrect: the article explicitly contrasts India's worst rank (175) on ambient air quality with a considerably better rank (88) on air pollution/emissions control, showing emission control gains don't automatically translate into cleaner air people breathe.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: India's efforts to clean its air need not slow its economic growth
questions.pyqLink: Tests static knowledge of index publishers/methodology, a recurring UPSC favourite (cf. questions on EPI, Global Innovation Index, HDI publishers).

questions.stem: With reference to cloud seeding, which one of the following best describes the technique and a key limitation associated with it, as seen in Delhi's trials?
options: It involves dispersing substances such as silver iodide or sodium chloride into clouds with sufficient existing moisture to induce precipitation, and its success depends on pre-existing favourable cloud conditions rather than guaranteeing rain in dry weather.
It involves releasing sulphate aerosols into the stratosphere to reflect solar radiation and lower global temperatures, a technique also known as solar radiation management.
It involves injecting carbon dioxide into underground saline aquifers for permanent sequestration, primarily used to cut industrial emissions.
It involves releasing biodegradable polymers into water bodies to absorb pollutants, commonly used to counter eutrophication.
questions.explanation: Cloud seeding introduces nucleating agents into clouds that already have adequate moisture to trigger precipitation; it cannot create rain from dry skies, which is why Delhi's October 2025 trial produced little to no rainfall. Options 2, 3 and 4 describe unrelated techniques — solar radiation management, carbon capture and storage, and water pollutant remediation respectively.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Delhi air pollution: How cloud seeding works — and doesn’t work
questions.pyqLink: Tests static science concept of weather modification technology, distinct from geoengineering/CCS techniques often confused with it.

questions.stem: A CAG performance audit on train derailments was cited in explaining the Sairang Express accident. With reference to the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The CAG is appointed by the President and holds office for a term of six years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
The CAG's audit mandate is confined to the accounts of the Union and State Governments and does not extend to autonomous bodies substantially financed by government grants.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly reflects Article 148's provisions on tenure. Statement 2 correctly reflects Article 151's procedure for laying CAG reports before Parliament. Statement 3 is incorrect — under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the CAG can also audit bodies substantially financed by government grants.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Sairang Express accident: What leads to train derailments?
questions.pyqLink: Tests constitutional provisions on CAG (Articles 148-151), a frequently tested static institution; similar to UPSC 2021 question on Union constitutional bodies.

questions.stem: The remake of 'Ramayan' has revived interest in the 1980s socio-political context surrounding Ramanand Sagar's TV serial. Consider the following statements about that period. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The locks of the disputed structure at Ayodhya were opened for Hindu worship in 1986, during Rajiv Gandhi's tenure as Prime Minister.
The Shah Bano case verdict of the Supreme Court concerned the right of a divorced Muslim woman to maintenance under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act was enacted in 1986, following the Shah Bano judgment.
questions.explanation: All three statements are historically accurate: the Ayodhya structure's locks were opened in 1986 under Rajiv Gandhi; the Shah Bano case (1985) upheld a divorced Muslim woman's right to maintenance under CrPC Section 125; and Parliament enacted the 1986 Act in response to the resulting political backlash. These interlinked events shaped the communal and electoral climate referenced in the article.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: How PM Rajiv Gandhi endorsed the making of ‘Ramayan’ — and lost power
questions.pyqLink: Tests static modern Indian history/polity intersection on the Shah Bano case and Ayodhya dispute timeline, a recurring theme in post-independence history questions.

questions.stem: The Sairang Express, involved in the Assam derailment, was operated by the Northeast Frontier Railway. Consider the following pairs of Railway Zones and their headquarters. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Northeast Frontier Railway (HQ Maligaon), East Coast Railway (HQ Bhubaneswar) and North Western Railway (HQ Jaipur) are correctly matched. South Western Railway's headquarters is Hubballi (Hubli), not Secunderabad — Secunderabad is the headquarters of South Central Railway, a common near-miss pairing.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Sairang Express accident: What leads to train derailments?
questions.pyqLink: Tests static knowledge of India's railway zone headquarters, a recurring geography/transport static-fact category.

questions.stem: With reference to the China-Pakistan joint military exercise Karakoram-2026, consider the following statements.
statements: Statement-I: The exercise was significant for India's security establishment because it was conducted in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, which borders both Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
Statement-II: China's Western Theatre Command of the People's Liberation Army oversees its military formations along the border with India.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct as per the article. Statement-II explains Statement-I's significance: because the exercise was held in Xinjiang under the Western Theatre Command's area of responsibility — the same command that oversees the India border — practising high-altitude, interoperable operations there has direct relevance for India's security calculus along Ladakh and J&K.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Karakoram-2026: How China and Pakistan are deepening military ties — and what it means for India
questions.pyqLink: Tests static knowledge of PLA's theatre command structure vis-a-vis India's border, relevant to India's neighbourhood security syllabus.

questions.stem: The Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), whose proposed levy on UPI transactions was recently put on hold, is a recurring term in India's digital payments landscape. With reference to the Indian economy, which one of the following best describes the term 'Merchant Discount Rate'?
options: The rate of interest charged by the Reserve Bank of India when it rediscounts commercial bills submitted by commercial banks
The fee paid by a merchant to the bank or payment network for enabling and processing a card or digital payment transaction, usually deducted as a percentage of the transaction value
The additional surcharge collected from a customer for making a payment through a foreign currency card
The commission paid by an issuing bank to the acquiring bank for maintaining a merchant's point-of-sale terminal
questions.explanation: MDR is the charge a merchant pays to banks/payment service providers for facilitating digital/card payment acceptance, deducted from the transaction amount — which is exactly why its proposed imposition on UPI P2M transactions drew objections from merchants. Option (a) confuses it with the Bank Rate; option (c) describes a cross-border currency conversion charge; option (d) describes interchange fee, a component of MDR but not MDR itself.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
questions.pyqLink: UPSC 2019: 'Which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate?' — same concept, now updated to the UPI context.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding Ebola Virus Disease, in the context of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo:
1. It is caused by viruses belonging to the family Filoviridae.
2. It is a zoonotic disease believed to spread to humans from infected fruit bats.
3. A vaccine has been approved and is in use against all known species of Ebolavirus, including the Bundibugyo virus.
4. Human-to-human transmission occurs mainly through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of infected persons.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: It is caused by viruses belonging to the family Filoviridae.
It is a zoonotic disease believed to spread to humans from infected fruit bats.
A vaccine has been approved and is in use against all known species of Ebolavirus, including the Bundibugyo virus.
Human-to-human transmission occurs mainly through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of infected persons.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are established facts about Ebola Virus Disease. Statement 3 is false: an approved vaccine (rVSV-ZEBOV) exists only for the Zaire ebolavirus species, which is why the article notes the Bundibugyo virus strain driving the current Congo outbreak has 'no known vaccine or treatment'.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
questions.pyqLink: Tests static biology of viral zoonotic diseases, a recurring GS Prelims theme (cf. Nipah, Zika PYQs).

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Empowered Committee (CEC) was originally constituted in 2002 on the orders of the Supreme Court and has since 2023 functioned as a statutory body.
2. Unscientific sand mining from active river channels can cause riverbed degradation, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquatic and riparian habitats.
3. The National Chambal Sanctuary is notified primarily for the protection of species such as the Gharial, Gangetic Dolphin and freshwater turtles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Central Empowered Committee (CEC) was originally constituted in 2002 on the orders of the Supreme Court and has since 2023 functioned as a statutory body.
Unscientific sand mining from active river channels can cause riverbed degradation, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquatic and riparian habitats.
The National Chambal Sanctuary is notified primarily for the protection of species such as the Gharial, Gangetic Dolphin and freshwater turtles.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. The CEC was set up in 2002 under Supreme Court orders and became a statutory body in 2023; the article explicitly lists riverbed degradation, groundwater depletion and habitat loss as impacts of unsustainable sand extraction; and the Chambal Sanctuary (the site of the CEC's sand-mining case) is a well-known riverine protected area for the critically endangered Gharial alongside the Gangetic Dolphin and turtles.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Central committee suggests three-year roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand mining from active river channels
questions.pyqLink: Tests river ecosystem ecology and statutory conservation bodies, similar to PYQs on Gharial/Chambal Sanctuary and the Supreme Court-mandated CEC.

questions.stem:
With reference to the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), consider the following statements:
1. It functions under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and was established under an Act of Parliament passed in 2021.
2. Its proposed registration framework provides only for permanent registration of qualified professionals and does not allow any provisional registration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: It functions under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and was established under an Act of Parliament passed in 2021.
Its proposed registration framework provides only for permanent registration of qualified professionals and does not allow any provisional registration.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the NCAHP operates under the Union Health Ministry and was created under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021. Statement 2 is incorrect: the article explicitly describes a draft framework for 'provisional registration' of allied and healthcare professionals with bridge courses to transition to regular registration, so provisional registration is very much a feature.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory/regulatory body category distinguishing allied healthcare professions regulation from the National Medical Commission — a recurring institutional-detail PYQ theme.

questions.stem:
Consider the following pairs regarding the latest Swachh Survekshan rankings:
City : Category in which it was ranked cleanest
1. Navi Mumbai : Cleanest city in India (overall)
2. Ujjain : Cleanest city in the 10 lakh-plus population category
3. Rewa : Cleanest riverfront town
4. Puri : Cleanest coastal town
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Cleanest city in the 10 lakh-plus population category
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched per the Swachh Survekshan results. Pair 2 is incorrect: Ujjain was ranked cleanest among cities with population between three and ten lakh, while Greater Visakhapatnam was the topper in the 10 lakh-plus population category.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Navi Mumbai recognised as India's cleanest city in latest Swachh Survekshan
questions.pyqLink: Tests familiarity with the Swachh Survekshan's multiple city-size and category-based rankings, a flagship scheme PYQ area (cf. Swachh Bharat Mission questions).

questions.stem:
The Himalayas feature in the news through an agenda proposal at COP31 by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan. Consider the following statements regarding the Himalayan region:
1. The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.
2. Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan are all landlocked countries.
3. The Hindu Kush Himalaya region is often called the 'Third Pole' because it holds the largest reserve of frozen water outside the polar regions.
4. Both the Indus and the Brahmaputra rivers originate on the Tibetan Plateau, north of the main Himalayan range.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.
Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan are all landlocked countries.
The Hindu Kush Himalaya region is often called the 'Third Pole' because it holds the largest reserve of frozen water outside the polar regions.
Both the Indus and the Brahmaputra rivers originate on the Tibetan Plateau, north of the main Himalayan range.
questions.explanation: All four statements are geographically accurate: the Himalayas are classic fold mountains from plate collision; Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan are all landlocked; the Hindu Kush Himalaya is termed the 'Third Pole' for its ice/snow reserves; and both the Indus and Brahmaputra rise near the Tibetan Plateau before diverging around the Himalayan arc.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
questions.pyqLink: Tests physical geography of the Himalayan mountain system and river origins, a recurring Prelims staple.

questions.stem:
With reference to the sidelining of the Himalayas agenda at COP31, consider the following:
Statement-I: The agenda item on the Himalayas proposed by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan was not included in the formal agenda of COP31.
Statement-II: Under the UNFCCC process, the formal agenda of a Conference of the Parties (COP) session is adopted only by consensus among Party blocs, so the lack of support from major blocs can keep a proposed item off the formal agenda.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is confirmed by the article: the Himalayas agenda failed to secure backing of developed-nation blocs and was left off COP31's formal list. Statement-II correctly explains this outcome, since COP decision-making, including agenda adoption, under the UNFCCC operates on consensus among Parties, meaning a lack of support from major blocs is sufficient to block formal inclusion of an agenda item.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
questions.pyqLink: Tests the consensus-based procedural architecture of the UNFCCC/COP process, similar to PYQs on climate conference mechanisms (Paris Agreement, CBDR).

questions.stem: A Telangana High Court bench recently directed a police commissioner to secure the presence of a District Collector in a contempt of court proceeding. With reference to the constitutional and statutory basis of the power to punish for contempt of court in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 129 of the Constitution declares the Supreme Court a "court of record" having all the powers of such a court, including the power to punish for contempt of itself, and Article 215 confers a similar status on every High Court.
Under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, truth can never be pleaded as a defence in contempt proceedings, regardless of public interest.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Articles 129 and 215 make the Supreme Court and High Courts "courts of record" with inherent contempt power, independent of the Contempt of Courts Act. Statement 2 is incorrect because the 2006 amendment inserted Section 13 into the Act, allowing truth as a valid defence if it is in the public interest and the request for invoking it is bona fide.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: HC directs Malkajgiri Police Commissioner to ‘ensure presence’ of Medchal Malkajgiri Collector before bench in contempt case
questions.pyqLink: Tests Articles 129/215 and the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 (2006 amendment) — a recurring static theme whenever a contempt case makes news.

questions.stem: During talks with a visiting Singapore delegation, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister referred to plans to generate 160 GW of renewable energy. With reference to India's climate and energy commitments, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: At COP26 (2021), India announced the "Panchamrit" targets, which include achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity by 2030.
India's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement target a reduction in the emissions intensity of GDP by 45% by 2030 compared to 1990 levels.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission is administered by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the Panchamrit targets at COP26 include 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030. Statement 3 is correct — MNRE, not the Ministry of Power, is the nodal ministry for the Green Hydrogen Mission. Statement 2 is incorrect because India's NDC baseline year for emissions intensity reduction is 2005, not 1990.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: CM Naidu urges Singapore to focus on integrated model township in Andhra Pradesh
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's COP26 Panchamrit pledges and NDC baseline year, a frequently tested static climate-economy theme.

questions.stem: The Tamil Nadu government recently ordered additional compensation to victims of the 2018 anti-Sterlite protests in Thoothukudi. With reference to the regulatory framework governing industrial pollution in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Sterlite copper smelter in Thoothukudi was ordered to be permanently closed by the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board in 2018 following protests over alleged air and groundwater pollution.
The National Green Tribunal is a statutory body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, to adjudicate environmental disputes.
The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 empowers State Pollution Control Boards to grant or refuse consent for the operation of industrial plants likely to cause air pollution.
Copper smelting is classified as a "white category" industry under the Central Pollution Control Board's classification, indicating minimal pollution potential.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the TNPCB ordered the Sterlite plant's closure in 2018, the NGT is indeed a statutory tribunal under the 2010 Act, and the 1981 Act gives State Boards consent powers over air-polluting industries. Statement 4 is incorrect — copper smelting is classified as a highly polluting "red category" industry, not "white category".
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Anti-Sterlite protests: CM orders ₹5.25-cr. additional relief to victims
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory pollution-control architecture (NGT Act 2010, Air Act 1981, CPCB industry colour-coding) behind the Sterlite episode.

questions.stem: The IMD has forecast that a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a "depression" by November 15. With reference to the India Meteorological Department's classification of low-pressure weather systems, which one of the following best describes a "depression"?
options: A low-pressure system located exclusively over land areas with no associated wind circulation
A cyclonic storm with maximum sustained surface wind speed between 62-88 km/h
A low-pressure area with associated maximum sustained surface wind speed of less than 31 km/h
A low-pressure system with maximum sustained surface wind speed in the range of 31-49 km/h
questions.explanation: The IMD classifies a "depression" as a low-pressure system with maximum sustained surface wind speed of 31-49 km/h (17-27 knots), one stage above a plain "low-pressure area" (below 31 km/h) and below a "cyclonic storm" (62-88 km/h). Option A describes no recognised IMD category, since all these systems are oceanic and involve organised wind circulation.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Depression over Bay of Bengal likely by November 15: IMD
questions.pyqLink: Tests the IMD's wind-speed-based classification of tropical low-pressure systems, a static meteorology concept behind recurring cyclone-season news.

questions.stem: The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education launched a new e-learning portal on the occasion of National Education Day, observed to mark the birth anniversary of India's first Education Minister. Consider the following pairs of national observance days and the personalities associated with them:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: National Education Day (November 11) correctly marks Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's birth anniversary, and National Science Day (February 28) correctly commemorates C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect. National Statistics Day (June 29) is actually linked to P.C. Mahalanobis, not Srinivasa Ramanujan, and National Unity Day (October 31) is linked to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, not Lal Bahadur Shastri. Hence only two pairs are correctly matched.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: APSCHE launches digital portal for accessible, self-paced learning
questions.pyqLink: Tests personality-observance day associations, a recurring static-current fusion format (cf. UPSC pairs-matched questions on commemorative days).

questions.stem: The Regional Meteorological Centre has forecast that a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal will bring rainfall to Tamil Nadu, which is currently facing a rain deficit. With reference to the northeast (retreating) monsoon over peninsular India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The northeast monsoon, which brings the bulk of annual rainfall to Tamil Nadu between October and December, develops as winds retreat from the Indian subcontinent and pick up moisture while crossing the Bay of Bengal.

Low-pressure systems and depressions that form over the Bay of Bengal during the northeast monsoon season frequently move westward or northwestward and make landfall along the Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coasts, contributing significantly to the season's rainfall.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The retreating/northeast monsoon forms as dry continental winds reverse direction after the southwest monsoon withdraws, gaining moisture over the Bay of Bengal before striking Tamil Nadu's east coast — explaining why Tamil Nadu, unlike most of India, gets its principal rainy season in winter. Bay of Bengal depressions in this season characteristically track west/northwestward onto this coast, which is precisely why such systems are being watched for relieving Tamil Nadu's rainfall deficit.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Low-pressure area likely to form over Bay of Bengal, ease rain deficit in State
questions.pyqLink: Tests the mechanism of the northeast/retreating monsoon and Bay of Bengal depression tracks — a classic Indian climatology theme.
